title: Search Infrastructure Comparison
subtitle: Evaluating Elasticsearch, Typesense, and Meilisearch for Acme Commerce

options.name: Elasticsearch
options.notes: Best fit for complex faceted search at our scale. Team has prior experience operating it.

options.name: Typesense
options.notes: Excellent performance and DX, but younger ecosystem. Worth revisiting in 12 months.

options.name: Meilisearch
options.notes: Simplest to deploy and great for small catalogs. Lacks features needed at our scale.

pros: Industry standard with 15+ years of production hardening
Excellent faceted search with aggregations and nested queries
Rich query DSL supporting complex filtering and boosting
Large ecosystem: Kibana, Logstash, APM, official clients in 20+ languages
cons: JVM-based, requires careful heap tuning and GC monitoring
High memory footprint, needs 8GB+ per node minimum
Operational overhead: cluster management, shard rebalancing, index lifecycle
Licensing changed after 7.10, SSPL concerns for some use cases

pros: Blazing fast, often sub-10ms for typical e-commerce queries
Built-in typo tolerance with customizable distance
Simple hosted option (Typesense Cloud) or self-hosted single binary
Clean REST API with great developer experience
cons: Younger project, smaller community and fewer integrations
No equivalent to Kibana for visualization and debugging
Limited clustering story for high availability
Team would need to learn new operational patterns

pros: Simplest setup of all three, single binary with no dependencies
Excellent indexing speed, handles 10M+ documents easily
Great typo tolerance out of the box with no configuration
Open source with permissive MIT license
Generous free tier on Meilisearch Cloud
cons: Faceted search is basic compared to Elasticsearch aggregations
No complex query DSL, limited filtering and boosting options
Smaller ecosystem, fewer client libraries and integrations
No built-in analytics or visualization tools
Not battle-tested at enterprise scale yet
